question: A teacher is currently four times as old as one of her students. Five years ago, she was seven times as old as the same student was at that time. What is the teacher’s current age (in years)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let student age = x ⇒ teacher = 4x

5 years ago: (4x − 5) = 7(x − 5)

⇒ 4x − 5 = 7x − 35

⇒ 30 = 3x ⇒ x = 10

**∴ Answer = 4x = 40 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Teacher is 4 times student. 5 years ago, teacher was 7 times student.

**Formula used:**

Linear equation formation based on age relation

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let student age = S, teacher age = T

⇒ T = 4S

⇒ 5 years ago: T − 5 = 7(S − 5)

⇒ Substitute T: 4S − 5 = 7S − 35

⇒ 30 = 3S ⇒ S = 10

⇒ T = 4 × 10 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Age Equation Formation

Present age relations translate directly into linear equations using variables.

Past Age Adjustment

For n years ago: subtract n from both present ages before forming ratio.

Ratio Concept

If A is k times B ⇒ A = kB, used to build equations quickly.

Linear Equation Solving

Bring variables to one side and constants to the other to isolate unknown.
